title: [Torch 4/11] Add Torch filtering, thresholding and signal-consistency vetoes
body:
Support Torch matched filtering, conditioning and signal-consistency vetoes.

## Standard information about the request

This is a: new feature.

This change affects: Torch-backed PyCBC workflows in the areas described below, with CPU compatibility coverage.

This change changes: the relevant backend implementation, tests and documentation. Torch is an optional dependency.

This change: includes focused unit tests. Validation scope is recorded below.

## Motivation

Torch-backed strain must pass through conditioning, correlation and signal-consistency checks before it can produce search triggers.

## Contents

Correlation, resampling and strain conditioning, threshold/clustering primitives, chi-square vetoes and Q-transform. Includes the existing 92-line phase-shift helper at its first caller; retains SciPy’s scalar optimizer. Uses existing native kernels without Cython changes. Timing regressions use resolved broadband peaks while preserving the original sine-wave overlap checks and tolerances.

Baseline formatting of existing Python files is inherited from [main formatting prerequisite](https://github.com/xangma/pycbc/pull/18); this PR owns the feature changes described above.

## Links to any issues or associated PRs

Depends on [#7](https://github.com/xangma/pycbc/pull/7) (`torch-pr3-psd`) at `b0855c9e5ed002777092735de7d02d64badc7245`. Main feature 4 of 11 in the 15-layer stack, including two formatting prerequisites and two optional feature branches.

Head branch: `torch-pr4-filtering`. Head commit: `0d6160c3ed22d87e63de4a0c663ac61038799cf4`. Base branch: `torch-pr3-psd`.

## Testing performed

The assembled large-batch rerun exposed a disabled-chi-square fallback bug, repaired in [#15](https://github.com/xangma/pycbc/pull/15) and validated at `efd63078f7211e7f1f428d1eaa4ec5a84a5aaf5f`. That repair is downstream of this intermediate PR. The prefix qualification below remains this PR's direct test record; completed rerun counts and final documentation checks are in #15.

Qualification at `0d6160c3ed22d87e63de4a0c663ac61038799cf4` on Linux used Python 3.11.9, Torch 2.13.0+cu130 and an RTX 4090, with native extensions rebuilt at each tested prefix. The owned test selection below recorded **355 passed, 55 skipped, plus 8 subtests** with `PYCBC_TEST_SCHEME=torch:cuda`. Qlty passed against this exact parent using `qlty check --no-upgrade-check --no-fix --sarif --no-progress --upstream b0855c9e5ed002777092735de7d02d64badc7245`.

The complete matched-filter suite also passed 10 tests and eight subtests on CPU and Torch CPU; the Torch CUDA run is included above.

```sh
PYCBC_TEST_SCHEME=torch:cuda python -m pytest -q -ra -p no:cacheprovider \
  test/test_matchedfilter.py \
  test/test_autochisq.py \
  test/test_chisq.py \
  test/test_chisq_torch.py \
  test/test_matched_filter_symm.py \
  test/test_qtransform.py \
  test/test_threshold.py \
  test/test_torch_chisq_cpu_optimization.py \
  test/test_torch_chisq_sparse_dispatch.py \
  test/test_torch_cpu_native_batch.py \
  test/test_torch_cuda_native_batch.py \
  test/test_torch_filter_pipeline.py \
  test/test_torch_matchedfilter_cpu_optimization.py \
  test/test_torch_search_kernels.py
```

The sine-wave timing fixture has a nearly flat correlation peak, so single-precision FFT roundoff overwhelms the curvature used for timing interpolation. Its failures reproduce on upstream CPU. The corrected timing fixture uses deterministic bandlimited noise at zero, half-record and positive/negative fractional shifts, in both precisions. The original match-value checks and timing tolerance remain; no production algorithm or test tolerance changed. This validates resolved peaks and does not promise accurate timing for nearly monochromatic signals.

Comprehensive MPS qualification and a full-site Sphinx build are not claimed.

The [assembled campaign](https://github.com/xangma/pycbc/tree/7f1ea7a7aa05b4fdafe2995a43a754984a2c5817) covers batches **1, 8, 32, 128, 512 and 1024** at main `4885b64560e9f39b740e85b6a976898869dd360e`, with optional CPU comparisons at `d544420232428225c214a4be84fbe1262a6d307b`. This intermediate PR was not separately retimed.

At batch 1024, the main default Torch CUDA route measured **52,984 work items/s**, versus **1,193** for the same-head standard CPU control, both with one host thread.

The synthetic live driver excludes waveform generation, PSD estimation, I/O and startup; chi-square is disabled, sine-Gaussian postprocessing is stubbed, and the unsafe asynchronous peak-copy route is disabled. It does not establish complete production-search speed.

[Benchmark documentation](https://github.com/xangma/pycbc/blob/dfd42bf76766cadca0eecf609a1eaeac73534676/docs/torch_optimization_results.rst) and [figure manifest](https://github.com/xangma/pycbc/blob/dfd42bf76766cadca0eecf609a1eaeac73534676/docs/images/torch-benchmarks-20260906/manifest.json).

This change: includes focused unit tests. Validation scope is recorded below.

## Motivation

Live search needs to turn Torch filter outputs into ranked events and serialized results through the existing search interfaces.

## Contents

Coincidence, ranking, cuts, significance, event management, live batch matching and StrainBuffer integration. Filtering primitives remain in the preceding PR.

title: [Torch 7/11] Add Torch TaylorF2 waveform family
body:
Generate the supported TaylorF2 waveform family with Torch.

## Standard information about the request

This is a: new feature.

This change affects: Torch-backed PyCBC workflows in the areas described below, with CPU compatibility coverage.

This change changes: the relevant backend implementation, tests and documentation. Torch is an optional dependency.

This change: includes focused unit tests. Validation scope is recorded below.

## Motivation

Torch search and inference need TaylorF2 templates that accept tensor parameters and frequency grids, with numerical parity and explicit precision boundaries.

## Contents

TaylorF2 variants, SPA template support, tidal helpers, batch generation and numerical parity tooling. The optional `PYCBC_TAYLORF2_TRITON=1` CUDA batch route fuses frequency evaluation while reusing existing validation, PN coefficients, reference phases, normalization, polarization rotation and per-row support. CPU, missing Triton, ROCm and reverse- or forward-mode gradient inputs use the ordinary Torch path. Selected compilation/launch failures propagate. New tests cover numerical edge cases, exact padding, gradient fallback and 65,536-row launch indexing.

Baseline formatting of existing Python files is inherited from [main formatting prerequisite](https://github.com/xangma/pycbc/pull/18); this PR owns the feature changes described above.

## Links to any issues or associated PRs

Depends on [#10](https://github.com/xangma/pycbc/pull/10) (`torch-pr6-waveform`) at `51e82b2ac935c53d988aae495f5e7c0328524b4e`. Main feature 7 of 11 in the 15-layer stack, including two formatting prerequisites and two optional feature branches.

Head branch: `torch-pr7-taylorf2`. Head commit: `a4ba198e7c4d2fa1b0238de946f1367a98e7a2f6`. Base branch: `torch-pr6-waveform`.

## Testing performed

title: [Torch 11/11] Add Torch validation and benchmark tooling
body:
Make Torch validation and benchmark results reproducible, with clearer guides, coverage through batch 1024 and a fix for live filtering with chi-square disabled.

## Standard information about the request

This is a: validation, documentation and bug fix.

This change affects: Torch-backed PyCBC workflows in the areas described below, with CPU compatibility coverage.

This change changes: CI workflows, validation guides, artifact tests, benchmark tooling and disabled-veto handling in live filtering.

This change: includes focused unit tests. Validation scope is recorded below.

## Motivation

Reproducible checks and benchmark artifacts show where the assembled backend is correct, when it falls back and which performance claims the measurements support.

## Contents

CPU/GPU selectors, artifact checks and benchmark tooling; eight simpler guides; a reproducible plot renderer; eight clearer figures and their provenance manifest; and `test/test_torch_large_batches.py`. Live and waveform figures separate CPU/1 thread, CPU/4 threads and CUDA/1 thread into three panels with different zero-based scales. Batched plots cover 1, 8, 32, 128, 512 and 1024. Single-vector FFT and single-evaluation inference figures retain their historical source revisions. Also guards disabled chi-square fallback materialization in `LiveBatchMatchedFilter._process_vetoes`, fixing the public live regression exposed by the new tests. Optional TaylorF2 Triton support is inherited from PR #11.

Baseline formatting of existing Python files is inherited from [main formatting prerequisite](https://github.com/xangma/pycbc/pull/18); this PR owns the feature changes described above.

## Links to any issues or associated PRs

Depends on [#14](https://github.com/xangma/pycbc/pull/14) (`torch-pr10-inference`) at `78d99b5e0f540abd438e01a221de77fc02109b3f`. Main feature 11 of 11 in the 15-layer stack, including two formatting prerequisites and two optional feature branches.

Head branch: `torch-pr11-performance-evidence`. Head commit: `dfd42bf76766cadca0eecf609a1eaeac73534676`. Base branch: `torch-pr10-inference`.

## Testing performed

Initial fixture import/alignment failures were corrected; subsequent runs exposed a disabled-chi-square fallback bug in `LiveBatchMatchedFilter._process_vetoes`. Original failed outcomes remain in the archive. The runtime guard fix was then tested in three clean source worktrees.

Completed repaired-source correctness: main `efd63078f7211e7f1f428d1eaa4ec5a84a5aaf5f` — **271 passed, 53 skipped**; optional FFT `bca6251a931fa2eaa0338485636c2cdbe6765b0b` — **344 passed, 53 skipped**; optional CPU `d90513f3956925b6fe368c2c57b16abb32bd822d` — **271 passed, 53 skipped**. Each selection executed 25 of 26 externally supplied large-batch regression cases, all passing; the sole skipped case requires CUDA and Triton and is intentionally skipped on CPU. Existing focused tests were included; FFT also included its three backend/wisdom test files. See [commands, environment, source IDs and JUnit](https://github.com/xangma/pycbc/tree/7f1ea7a7aa05b4fdafe2995a43a754984a2c5817/batch1024/correctness). Each repaired source is a child of its respective immutable benchmark source, with only the runtime guard changed. The final candidates carry the respective tested runtime file bytes, documentation, plot renderer and identical regression file. These correctness runs were not repeated at the final candidate commits. Qlty is unavailable locally; no new Qlty result is claimed for the runtime repair.

The final documentation passed focused Sphinx validation with warnings as errors: all 11 Torch pages, internal references, eight figure hashes and the downloadable manifest. External document targets were verified and stubbed; the full site was not built. The receipt binds the current page and manifest hashes; the manifest binds the renderer and figures.

The new regression file is supplied externally when testing clean main, FFT and optional CPU sources before the documentation amendment.

Qualification on the prior head `d44ed6e2273488b0fcd52819f3a604ae38b8a79c` used Python 3.11.9, Torch 2.13.0+cu130 and an RTX 4090, with native extensions rebuilt at each tested prefix. The owned test selection below recorded **114 passed, 2 skipped** with `PYCBC_TEST_SCHEME=torch:cuda PYCBC_TAYLORF2_TRITON=1`. Qlty passed against this exact parent using `qlty check --no-upgrade-check --no-fix --sarif --no-progress --upstream 78d99b5e0f540abd438e01a221de77fc02109b3f`.

Compatibility checks at the pre-Triton baseline `607bce53ead14f12af32552a5b2441d3bc667267` recorded **1,436 passed, two skipped, plus eight subtests** across the core/domain selections. The domain selection initially hit CUDA allocation failure under unrelated GPU load and passed its full rerun with capacity available. Complete matched-filter checks passed 10 tests and eight subtests on CPU, Torch CPU and Torch CUDA. The same `d44ed6e22734` source separately passed **58 TaylorF2 tests, four skipped**, the exact CI F401 gate and the main-extension scope check. The broader compatibility counts above were not rerun after Triton.

The non-blocking CUDA peak-copy race remains unresolved: delayed-stream probes failed immediate reads on published and rebuilt PR5 heads with identical code. Synchronization corrected all three arrays; blocking copies were correct immediately.

```sh
PYCBC_TEST_SCHEME=torch:cuda PYCBC_TAYLORF2_TRITON=1 python -m pytest -q -ra -p no:cacheprovider \
  test/test_torch_performance_artifacts.py \
  test/test_torch_parity_artifacts.py
```
